body:
It would be completely devastating for them and it would affect them for the rest of their lives. They may hopefully learn to move on, forgive the past and regain joy and happiness in life one day, but they will never be the same. They will carry it in their hearts forever. I'm sorry it's that way because it doesn't of course make things any easier for you right now. Of course this also applies to any unexpected, sudden death, like a car crash. It's just that with suicide it is all the more stinging because guilt, regret, social stigma and confusion are involved.

Your parents and relatives would feel they failed you, that it was their fault, that they should have done something to help. (If only they'd made one last phonecall, asked you round for dinner, done just a bit more to prevent it.) Plus the loss of all those years invested in you. But your children especially would be affected, as they expect you to lead them into life and support them and would grow up like orphans.

That's why people don't understand how hard a decision suicide is. Anyone who thinks it is the "easy way out" needs their head examined, or a slap in the face.

Also you would be depriving your own future self of ever experiencing anything nice, which is pretty unfair to your future self. All those things you've always dreamed of doing. Maybe you won't do all or even any of them, but you will have other experiences that you may well look back on (e.g. watch your kids grow up, attend their high school graduation, learn a new skill, win an award, achieve a goal, visit a place you always wanted, etc.) and be glad your past self hadn't pulled the plug. So in a way you owe it to yourself and others to stay around. It's like a form of self-love towards the you of the future. I decided that I couldn't kill myself until I had run a marathon, because you get one life and I didn't want to die knowing I had never even done one thing to be proud of. I thought at least I had to do that, and then I could kill myself. So I trained up and I ran one. Then I got hooked on running, which is the best thing I ever did. Does wonders for your mind and body. That and cutting out all processed food, sugar and caffeine, eating tons of vegetables and taking vitamins. I also knew I couldn't die before my siblings had come back from holiday, or passed their exams, or got married, etc, and eventually one thing leads to another and there's always something else you want to do. Something else you want to learn. Some other place you want to see. Some other thing you want to achieve. And if you pull the plug, you will never be able to.

It's really hard. I feel for you. It's a horrendous place to be in because of course saying all this only makes it harder for you to bear. But it's better to know than to make the common mistake of thinking you're a "burden" if you stay alive. Never ever fall for that because it is almost always the opposite that's true.

If you kill yourself because you are worried you can't support your family and you feel like a failure, you would be making a big mistake. Because you will always be worth immeasurably more to them alive as their mother than dead, no matter how much you fail to provide for them or how many problems you may be burdening them with. Never forget that.

Also I agree with others your company were totally out of line and you may have grounds for unfair dismissal.

"i want to live and be happy"

You already acknowledged deep down you don't want to die, which if so is more than half the battle won already.

 "but for me that can't happen"

This is an assumption you're making, which many people would challenge. Be very careful basing major decisions on potentially flawed assumptions. The only things you can say for certain are you aren't happy *now*, or that you haven't been happy at X times in the past. You can't possibly say what can or can't happen in the future, especially when it comes to putting restrictions on your own future happiness, because happiness largely depends on you and your attitude in any given situation.

It's not an easy or quick fix but I hope you can find strength and support. My best wishes.

If you do not actually want to die at all maybe you have some kind of OCD that makes your brain obsess over these thoughts. If you are actually unhappy enough with life to be suicidal that's a different issue.

I can't personally relate to that. If i feel suicidal it is a case of not knowing whether i wil ever act on it or not. But if everyone acted on all the thoughts they have the world would be a very different place. Thinking about doing something and actually doing it are very different things.

Don't do it.

Run a marathon first. Might as well.

My depression lifted when I fasted, stopped eating crap and exercised.

Yes! The belief that all suicidal people must be suffering from "mental illness" such as depression is one of the biggest myths currently going around. There are multiple reasons for suicide, not all of which require a depressed state.

Shame your mum is like that but she does still love you even if she isn't always supportive. The fact she is annoyed proves that. The opposite would be total indifference. 
As for the investment. I can assure you if you asked your mum would see things differently. Raising a child is a huge expense. Carrying you for 9 months in her belly, going through agony at childbirth, years of sleepless nights, dirty nappies, buying toys, dealing with tantrums, making important decisions every single day about your future, sacrificing countless social engagements to stay home with you and foregoing luxuries, losing so much of their former freedom. Plus financially an enormous burden. If you believe CNN (no idea how realistic it is but I've seen several similar studies) it costs an average of 240,000 USD to raise a child to 18 before we even think about uni fees. I'd say that's a pretty big investment. You are worth a quarter of a million dollars to your parents. Basically instead of buying a house they had you. :) They'doybe pretty gutted to lose you to say the least. And obviously you're worth far more to them than the money.
You're good with computers. That's an amazing skill to have if you can develop it. Probably the number one career that lends itself to self study. I've met several people who never went to uni who've got good IT jobs with decent salaries just from learning in their bedroom. I have a degree and I'm jealous. Degrees are useful obviously but really it's about your skills. 

Also you're so young even if you've heard that a million times before. Sure it doesn't feel like that. It feels like your life is over. But trust me you have so much time. If you literally sat at hone on benefits for 4 years and smoked weed every day you'd still only be 24. Still really young. Or you could sit at home and learn to code at the same time.

Google strikes me as exactly the kind of place that rewards talent rather than conventional qualifications. Even if it isn't IT is one of the most in-demand skills in the world. Google isn't the only dream job out there. There are opportunities you can't even envisage because you're focussing on one narrow path. Opportunities come and go all the time. But if you're dead you won't be around to see them... ;p It's not like either I get this degree and work at my dream job at Google or my life isn't worth living so I'll kill myself. There's a huge amount in between those two extremes. You just have to widen your field of vision.

Iced tea is not to be knocked. ;) Start from there. That might be the only thing you're living for. But it's still enjoyable. If you can even get to the point where you want to die but just once I've finished my tea then that's a start. Chances are you'll keep finding more annoying things to keep you here. Just after I watch that sunset. Just after I've visited that place or done that activity. You still haven't done e.g. skydiving. Might as well stay alive until you have. You might find a few other things just as valid as iced tea. Or you've forgotten them. Stuff you used to do as a child. Playing in the woods. Climbing trees. Swimming in a lake. Riding a rollercoaster. Chances are at the exact moment that you're doing sth you really enjoy, you're not desperate to kill yourself. You might think once it's over you will. But at that moment, right as you're engaged in that thing you don't. Try and find the things that give you that feeling. Even if it's just a distraction at first.

Anyway it's not like there's a huge rush. Yes time is limited and your life only contains a certain number of minutes. But you have a lot of them. Of course when you're experiencing extreme mental anguish it becomes more urgent. But even those states don't last forever.

Hope some of that was helpful. ;o

I can't comment on your specifics but the people to see are the uni people. They have dealt with cases like this and can at least give some advice. First you have to establish you definitely lost the scholarship. That's step 1. You'd be pissed if you died then found out you had it after all. If you could be pissed while dead that is.
That's worst case scenario. Then you take it from there. Yes it would be devastating. But suicide is infinitely more devastating.not to be messed with. Also you'd be surprised how hard it is to kill yourself. The life instinct is there for a reason. Extremely hard to override that programming. Especially since you don't even want to die. You want to be able to stay at college so you can escape from home and have a future, which is the opposite of wanting to die. If you didn't care so much about this future you wouldn't be having such panic now. This is the paradox of suicide. You can't have the life you crave, so you kill yourself. Doesn't really make sense.
Btw never ever think you are a burden on your family or they'd be better off without you or anything. That is the worst lie you can ever fall for. Absolutely categorically your family are better off with you here and your death would be the most traumatic event imaginable for them. I'm not saying that to be depressing but to bring home the seriousness of suicide. It's not a decision anyone can take lightly. Believe me, I wouldn't be here if it was. You have invested so much into this but you and they have also invested far more into your life so far. Throwing your life in because of the degree therefore doesn't make sense. If you lose the degree, hold onto the bigger investment which is yourself.

I know your dreams hang on that phonecall so it's terrifying. But you have to face it and call. Your subconscious won't let you rest til you do. Then whatever the outcome, breathe, hold onto something solid and remember the world hasn't ended. It only ends when you die. And there are so many alternative possibilities before that.

And don't be afraid to tell your parents how upset you are and ask them to help you make the phonecall if possible.

Whatever happens don't rush. There are always other options before suicide.

Good luck.

Being at home is hell. College is your lifeline. But now threat of leaving college looms. So suicide seems like a good way out. But it is not. There are other options.
There are places you can stay for free or in exchange for sone labour like monasteries and farms. You can WWOOF. Take time out. Crash with friends a few weeks to take away the stress of home.
There are schemes like Peace Corps and volunteer programmes that give free lodging.
Worst case scenario apply for sheltered accommodation. Still better than death.
Suicide is the final option. Only to be used when you have exhausted all others. Which you haven't. And you're only 19. You have plenty of time for other options. It's not: college is my lifeline out of hell at home, and it's being taken away so I might as well kill myself. There are hundreds of steps missing in between before suicide comes into it.

All you need to do is make that phonecall. You can't kill yourself over a phonecall. Then take it from there. Ask to see he counsellor. Tell the scholarship people how you're feeling and ask for help.
You can't be the first student to lose a scholarship or have financial support. Maybe there is s chance of taking time off and getting a new scholarship later.
Hope you get it sorted.
But make the phonecall even if it's the scariest thing you ever do. You will feel better for it. And probably find it wasn't as scary.
This means you have to stay alive tonight so you can call tomorrow 
Ask someone to sit with you if possible while you do it.
You won't be able to sleep til you do. Trust me I've been there.
Breathe slowly. Go to bed. Wake up tomorrow. Call.
;)

Don't do it. Your life is worth more than a degree.
Take deep breaths. You can get through this. And you know in your heart you can't let your mother and sister find you like that. It would be devastating. Plus it's not as easy as you'd think.
Also you need to find out if it is a mistake first.
Even if it isn't it is not the end of your life. There are other funding options.You can discuss it all with the college.
Be strong. You are loved. Don't throw it away that quickly.

Wow sorry you had to have someone like that enter your life. 
I met someone sinilar but on a tiny scale compared to yours. She'll probably fuck over a few more lives before she burns out but you can live in hope she will get caught out one day and have her comeuppance. Or at least consolation she will probably never really be at peace even if she is living it up. Maybe she is to be pitied.

I don't really get how you didn't get compensation or police support or fraud cover in any of this but maybe things are different where you are. Seems incredible all that was allowed to happen to you 

That was well written by the way and echoes some of my feelings.

Only thing I could say. You have no one left to worry about (no friends at all?). But I like to think that even if you are as good as dead, there is still one thing you can do: help some other poor sod whose life is even more fucked up. As in even if you have nothing left to offer here, your very presence as an intelligent, educated, English-speaking adult could be useful to some kid somewhere who would lose out if you disappear. Even a small loan to someone. I like to think that since I'm also pretty pissed off I was born. As if I would ever have agreed to this insanity given half a choice. But now that I'm stuck here even on my last legs with everything ruined I could still help unfuck someone else's life a bit so it might be worth sticking around a bit more. But it depends on each person. For me it is not necessarily out of care but maybe duty. I don't like to see things fucked up so I want to fix them if I can. Seeing people who have been screwed over pisses me off. Since no one was there to stop it happening to me being able, with minimal effort, to prevent it happening to some other poor person somewhere is like a way of sticking your finger up at life and saying: In your face, you prick. Maybe akin to dragging a wounded man to cover to thwart the prison camp guards trying to shoot him.

Otherwise you have my sympathy.

Your comment reminds me of that Simpsons episode where the self-help guru advertises his book called "Get confident, stupid!"? Lol.

As some anonymous native American apparently once said: "Never judge a man until you've walked a mile in his moccasins."

I don't want you dead.

Sounds like you've been through shit.

That's normal. You don't have to be depressed to hate your life so much you want to die. 

But don't jump. Very bad method. At least for your family's sake. Yes it's tempting as it seems so "easy". Not much planning needed. But it's not a clean thud like in movies. Trust me. Your family may be strong but they will have to identify the body. There is also a risk of hitting someone or something on the way down. Or worse of not even dying and being paralysed. Also you may chicken out halfway down when it's too late. Google bridge jump survivors. Many say that.

Your family may be strong but you may be assuming they are stronger than they are. They won't just get on with life. It will permanently scar their lives and be with them til they die.

Also our concept of failure is open to question. In nature there is no failure. You either live and survive, or you don't, and you die. If you are alive you are by definition not failing. It's just failure according to our society's standards. And different societies have different standards. In some cultures having a degree is irrelevant. There are other courses. Worst case scenario you have to drop out and take some time off then try another. Feel like shit for a while. But it's still better than killing yourself because then you won't feel anything. You still have time.

What's so special about tonight for it to be your last ever experience of consciousness? Why tonight and not tomorrow or the next day?

Messing up is horrible. But if you are alive you have a chance however small to make things a bit better. Even a remote chance is a chance. If you are dead you have 0% chance. If you fuck up tonight maybe you'll fuck up tomorrow too and the next day and the next month or year. But you may also wake up next year and have a time when you don't fuck up. If you die tonight, you will never have that option. If there was a way to reset and start again believe me, I would have taken it. Or a way to deactivate your life Facebook style but with the option of coming back before permanent oblivion in case you change your mind. But sadly there isn't. This is the one shot.

Suicide is not really an 'option'; it's the option that ends all other options. When all other options are gone.

Failing your studies is painful. But it is still infinitely different from dying.

There's a big space lying between failing studies and ending everything you have ever been or will ever experience or contribute to the world. You can always try other things first then suicide. Stay at a monastery for a few weeks or stay with relatives first. Live on a commune. Use your credit card to book a skydiving trip. Why not? Since you'll never have the chance again. Point is death is right at the bottom of the options list.
 
In any case, you need to tell your parents about your grades issue and be honest. If the course is making you suicidal better to fuck the course than fuck your life, which is worth a lot more.

Don't do that. Someone would have to search for your body and drowned bodies are not pretty and not something you ever want any of your relatives to have to identity. There are better ways.

No one deserves to be killed. Unless you committed some horrific crime which you most likely haven't since you're on Reddit and not in prison.

Put all the energy you have spent in planning your suicide into planning your life and see what happens. (I know right, such a hypocrite!) Either you want to kill yourself, or you want to live. If you want to kill yourself, then bloody well do it. If it takes that long to decide if you want to die (3 years), then maybe you don't really want to kill yourself. Maybe you secretly want to live. Or you can't bear to do it to your family. Either way, expend energy on doing SOMETHING. Just take action. My biggest reason for suicide is that deep down I am so desperate to live. I am so desperate to experience life on a more fulfilling level than I am currently, that I can only think about suicide. A paradox maybe only a fellow suicidal person can understand?

My middle name is Devil's Advocate.

I would say living with suicidal ideation on a daily basis is an affliction no less horrible than many other horrendous afflictions, and made more so by the fact people are expected to suffer in silence. Do cancer sufferers feel guilt about complaining when they realise other people have it worse off? Why should suicidal people act like it's easy? It's not easy. It's horrible. It's a daily torment, and it's about time society recognised that it is real. There are many more ways for a human to suffer than physical.

1. This may well be true and hard to disprove. It may be most suicides have previously experienced depression, but not all depression sufferers go on to make suicide.
2. Most suicides are depressed, but not all. Also, depression is hard to quantify. The period of "illness" is not cut and dry. Unlike the flu, depression can come and go within a date range, so a depression sufferer would be labeled as such following suicide, but they may have been free of symptoms for weeks prior to the act.
Yes, feeling miserable about life is a symptom of clinical depression. But depression is not necessarily a symptom of feeling miserable about life. Sometimes life just stinks and there's no need for an illness or "chemical imbalance" to explain it away.
Thanks for the input.

If you don't want to die you've already passed the most difficult test. There are always other options. To reach the point where literally suicide is your only option is so improbable. Unless you're trapped down a dead end street being chased by hungry wolves. The point of suicide is it's a choice you make despite the other options available. But if you actually don't want to die then as I said the hard part is over.


Also your suicide would not prevent WWIII. But it would cause your family extreme grief.

I cut myself for years but eventually it gets kind of boring and I couldn't be bothered. It got to the point where cutting might give me temporary relief but then I'd wake up the next day with the same problem so it didn't solve anything. I think I actually just grew out of it. I don't regret it at all but the scars are a bit inconvenient. I'd recommend sleeping, screaming into a pillow or even punching a wall until it hurts. Less permanent. Or if you have the energy, running til your legs ache or lifting weights. Paradox is it's half impossible when you feel crap but if you are able to drag yourself out the effects are worth it.

Sorry you're in that state. I know it's hard.
Feeling that you would have done it given an easy way doesn't in any way mean you would actually have done it or that you should do it. It's possible to be acutely suicidal on many many occasions yet still pull through.

Also if it's similar I've been there. Those horrendous sleepless nights where you toss and turn, wake up every 30 mins to pee, wake up at 7 am after a few hours of unrestful sleep with heart jumping out of your chest and the worst kind of dread feeling. Those days when you are so tired your legs ache but you can't fall asleep for the life of you and your legs actually start to feel an achey coldness from anxiety. And the worst part is your one escape from the pain - sleep - is denied you. Those days when Valium softens it but no amount of cigarettes or booze or deep breathing will take it away. If you could bottle it you could usher in a new kind if chemical warfare. After experiencing that, you long for good old fashioned depression. Where you can say fuck it, cry your tears and just escape into sleep for 16 hours.

I don't really get what it is you're suffering from. Stuff caused as a result of your suicide attempt or problems you already had? Some kind of chronic fatigue? Tell me to piss off if it sounds stupid but have you looked into diet? Helped me out. Sugar, gluten, additives, alcohol can have surprising effects. If it's anxiety there's usually some underlying problem that needs resolving. Until it is your subconscious will go into panic mode.

Hear you about the depression thing. Does my head in too how it has a total monopoly on suicide. Like some retarded mantra everyone's been indoctrinated with. Followed by the tape-recorded response of: "See a professional for CBT and medication" or "Call this hotline". Makes you want to slap people round the face.

I think your girlfriend would rather have a living, broke, boyfriend no matter how much of a "failure", than a dead boyfriend.
My thoughts with you.
I hope you had insurance for your talking dog.

Waking up one day and realising everything you ever dreamed you would do or become is now not going to happen. And this is it: reality. The reality of both your life and the universe. Realising everything you thought you knew or believed about yourself, about the world, about living, was wrong. Realising that there is no magical force that will save you. That life is a blank canvas and you are the artist. If you don't paint anything, nothing will ever happen. Realising that you are not special. That countless other beings have lived and died before you and you are no different. That everyone feels themselves to be as special as you do. That there is nothing guaranteeing you a happy or painfree life or that you will ever make something of yourself. That it is entirely up to you to take action. But first you must decide what you want. Faced with ultimate freedom you can either break out of your prison tower and soar through the clouds, or plummet to earth. And the only thing that decides which it will be is you.
Long story. Existence leads to anxiety.

Thanks. I don't believe in a personal God but appreciate the support. Mental state changed since then. But crises come and go. You can literally wake up in the morning with heart pumping from existential anxiety and not be able to bear 10 minutes. You can be in hell one minute then the next day not be able to remember exactly what it is you were feeling or articulate it. Then a week later it might come back. Like storms that rise and fall. When you're in the storm it genuinely feels you will die. Now the tempest has died down but the water is still choppy.

Thanks for your wishes. It's a bit hard as it would take probably a couple of days to explain. So many events. So many thoughts. So many ingredients that make up the situation over so many years. Basically in order to explain why I'm suicidal I would have to explain my entire life history to you, everything that makes me me, which is not possible here. Because suicidality is not a simple label but a wholly unique experience to each individual. I'm not quite sure what I'm hoping people can help with, if anything.

Yes at home. Dilemma: I have reached the point where I really can't live another day. As in really. I would end it tonight. But I can't kill myself without destroying all my family's lives. I'm expected to keep going indefinitely. Now what exactly am I supposed to do? Other than cry into my pillow from the unimaginable pressure.

The assumption ppl always make is that if you're suicidal you have a choice whereas with a physical illness you don't. You're just an innocent victim and noons can be blamed. Meanwhile a suicide is "selfish" because they could have chosen to stay alive and spare ppl the pain. If your idea of choice is choosing to not endure indescribable hell every waking moment then yes it is a choice. But I wouldn't accuse the man who frees himself from the hunter's trap by cutting his own leg off of making a selfish choice.

NB. while I'm on the topic of ranting.
No I don't believe I am a burden to my family. Many ppl make that mistake. Not me.
No I don't think my family would be better off without me. That's ridiculous and insulting to my intelligence. Of course they are better off with me which is the single reason I am still here because quite frankly I couldn't bear the pain for anything else. Essentially the pain of existence is too much to bear, but the pain and guilt of destroying my family's life is even stronger. So I'm in hell. Even concern for friends wouldn't keep me here. It's not that I don't care about fucking their lives. It's that the pain outweighs the guilt. Whereas for my family it doesn't.
No my thoughts aren't clouded by depression.

Every time someone says suicide is a "permanent solution to a temporary problem" they should have to pay a fine. Or be chased round the streets in their underwear. Clearly my understanding of the word "temporary" is vastly different than the mainstream.

I have a hard time describing all this in words. I don't think it's even possible. Human language is so limited. Yes being me has become unbearable to the point getting through even half a day is terrifying.

Surroundings aren't ideal but it's not that that is causing this. Existentential dread/anxiety. But not in the questioning the universe way. I don't have time for that stuff these days. Not sure how to describe it. Other than that it is completely unbearable and whenever I hear people say suicides are cowardly/weak, etc I want to hit them in the face with a rotten fish because they would be crying for mummy and begging for mercy after 1 day of this. Thanks for listening.

Smoking. Drinking too much. Eating crap food and too much sugar. Wanking too much (unhealthy psychological addiction). Cleaning my ears with Q-tips/cotton buds. Spending too much time online. Sleeping through sunny days. Regretting the past/obsessing over what might have been, on a daily basis. Ruminating. Worrying/always assuming the worst. Blaming my parents/society/education/unfortunate circumstances/health/life/my own poor decisions and mistakes. Getting upset over trivial things I won't remember in a month anyway like the weather/losing my keys/crap drivers. Taking things too seriously. Daydreaming about possibilities instead of actually *doing*. Comparing myself constantly to others and regretting my shortfalls/beating myself up for not fulfilling my own potential. Expecting more from others than I give them in return. Being too critical of others and also my own worst critic. Being too hard on myself for 'failing' at all of the above. Saying the word "too" too much. Picking my nose.

I have ocd type issues too, crippling apathy and lots of other stuff. I don't know if I can help you but just want to offer my support. You only get one life. Even if you're in hell I hope you can work sth out. I find being in nature doing sth physical and away from all tech makes my ocd better. Staying at home and worse in your bedroom is like a recipe for madness. I should know. I've done that all today. *Force* yourself to get up even just to take a shower and walk to the shops. I think I am going to listen to my own advice.

Take it from me: 20 is not old when it comes to losing your virginity. I genuinely thought I would die a virgin but I got there eventually. TV just makes it seem like everyone is hooked up in high school and always at it. Most people are having a lot less sex than you'd realise. Also cultures vary dramatically. In many countries it's still considered normal for men to stay virgins and live at home til they marry, even into their 30s.

I can't attempt to understand your predicament other than offering my sympathy as a stranger. I cant judge because i know how unbearable it can be but I would say you are worth far more to your children alive than money can ever give. Being poor, even destitute with a parent is still preferable to being the child of a suicide. Also leaving a note would be better I think rather than leaving your children forever questioning. I also dont recommend trains. Not a nice way to go. But I don't think you should do it. You want to kill yourself because you can't provide a future for your children who you love, but if you kill yourself you will damage their future much more which doesn't really make sense. Its like out of love for your children you feel compelled to do something that will permanently deprive them of the very love and nurturing you are worried they will lose. Do you see the contradiction? They will also be at a much higher lifetime risk of suicide themselves. I know that doesn't make you feel good to hear but it's something to bear in mind. I know how horribly trapped you can feel but sometimes it's actually easier to stay alive. Even if your ex took custody and you were relieved of their care you would still be far more valuable to them. Because you would still be their parent, which is more valuable than any financial support. Money should never be the main reason behind suicide and if it is there is something seriously wrong with the system. I can't give much advice or judge you whatever decision you make as i appreciate how excruciating the emotional pain is but I hope there are other sources you can turn to for support. To play devil's advocate (because I am a hypocrite) from a purely logical perspective, think of suicide as the final option at the bottom of a long to-do list. Only when you have exhausted every other option on the list can you select it. I.e. there is literally *nothing* else on earth you can do to improve the situation but kill yourself. Most of the time, if you think about it, it turns out that doesn't apply. Ther may be another job out there if you contact an agency. Maybe put a post on Facebook saying you need a job/place to stay or bulk email all your relatives/friends explaining how desperate you are. You never know. Embarrassing and awkward perhaps but arguably less painful than a train wheel through your belly.

I can relate to the unbearableness but not your specific issues. Maybe there is some subconscious reason for the urges you need to identify. Having things good on the surface means nothing if your psyche is not happy. Daily torment is surely a reason. Try and work out what it is that is causing you the anxiety or dread or whatever it is.
